title: "ECONS 431 Computational Economics"
subtitle: "Washington State University"

---

Computational tools for solving and analyzing economic models: programming in
Python, working with economic data, numerical methods, microeconomic
applications, estimation, and agent-based modeling.

## Start here

1. **Set up your codespace** with the [Setup guide](setup.qmd) before the second
   class session. It runs in your web browser, so there's nothing to install.
2. **Stuck?** Check the [Setup FAQ](setup-faq.qmd), then post on Discussions.
3. **Each week**, the [Schedule](schedule.qmd) links that week's readings and
   lecture notebooks.

## Where things live

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Lecture notes, notebooks, readings, setup help | This site |
| Your problem sets | Your private repo: `WSU-EconS431/ps-<your-username>` |
